modern: As to living in the best way, this power is in the soul, if it is indifferent to things that are indifferent. And it will be indifferent if it looks at each of these things both separately and as a whole, and if it remembers that not one of them produces in us an opinion about itself, nor comes to us; but these things stay still, and it is we ourselves who produce the judgements about them and, as we might say, write them in ourselves, when it is in our power not to write them, and in our power, if by chance these judgements have slipped unnoticed into our minds, to wipe them out; and if it remembers too that such attention will only be needed for a short time, and then life will be over. Besides, what trouble is there at all in doing this? For if these things are according to nature, rejoice in them and they will be easy for you: but if they are contrary to nature, look for what is in keeping with your own nature, and strive towards this, even if it brings no reputation; for every man is allowed to seek his own good.
original: As to living in the best way, this power is in the soul, if it be indifferent to things which are indifferent. And it will be indifferent, if it looks on each of these things separately and all together, and if it remembers that not one of them produces in us an opinion about itself, nor comes to us; but these things remain immovable, and it is we ourselves who produce the judgments about them, and, as we may say, write them in ourselves, it being in our power not to write them, and it being in our power, if perchance these judgments have imperceptibly got admission to our minds, to wipe them out; and if we remember also that such attention will only be for a short time, and then life will be at an end. Besides, what trouble is there at all in doing this? For if these things are according to nature, rejoice in them and they will be easy to thee: but if contrary to nature, seek what is conformable to thy own nature, and strive towards this, even if it bring no reputation; for every man is allowed to seek his own good.

explained.summary:
The power to live well is already in your own mind, as long as you stay neutral about things that are neither good nor bad in themselves, like money, status and comfort. Look at each such thing on its own and as part of the whole, and remember that it doesn’t push an opinion into you. The things just sit there; you write the judgements about them into yourself, and you can decline to write them, or rub them out if they slip in.

Marcus adds that this effort is only needed for a short while, since life ends soon. If something suits your nature, enjoy it; if not, look for what does, even if it brings no reputation.
explained.today: A rainy bank holiday, a cancelled train or a poor exam result arrives without a verdict attached. ’This has ruined everything’ is a line you add yourself. Catch it as you’re writing it, and you can cross it out and simply get on with the next thing.
